texts.preamble: Maneesh K.S vs Umesha on 13 October, 2025 Kabc020351622022 Before The Court Of 10th Additional Small Causes And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, At: Bengaluru (Scch-16) Present: Sri. Mohammed Yunus Athani B.A.,Ll.B., X Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Mact, Bengaluru.
texts.facts: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondent, on account of grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the case are as follows: On 20-06-2022 at about 7.35 p.m., the petitioner was a pedestrian and in order to cross the road, he was standing carefully, by following all the traffic rules, near Bengaluru-Tumkur NH-48 service road, Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, Subash Nagara, Bengaluru District, Karnataka. At that time, the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-04-HN- 1470 came from Nelamangala to Bengaluru, with high speed, in rash and negligent manner, endangering the human life, recklessly, unmindfully, without following the traffic rules and without observing the movement of pedestrians and dashed against the petitioner. Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body. Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Matrushree Hospital, thereafter he was shifted to Aditya Orthopaedic and Trauma Centre, Tumkur, wherein he took treatment as an in-patient. Earlier to the accident, he was student and also working as electrician and earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month. But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity. The Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered the case against the rider of the said motorcycle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 338 of I.P.C. The respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 18% per annum. 3. On service of notice to the respondent, the respondent has appeared through his counsel and filed the written statement. 4. The respondent in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. He has contended that, the petitioner who was a motorcycle rider in NH-48 had parked his bike on the road side and had jumped the barricade to pass urinals in the service road. After passing the urinals near a tree in the service road, the petitioner who was in a hurry to cross the road did not notice the respondent's bike coming on the service road and ran towards the NH-48. The respondent was driving his motorcycle with helmet and all safety measures in the service road, at about 30 to 40 km speed, along with a pillion rider. The petitioner became a sudden obstacle to the respondent's bike, for which the respondent could not control his vehicle and dashed the petitioner, who was in hurry to cross the road. Both the petitioner and respondent have sustained injuries. The respondent had Maneesh K.S vs Umesha on 13 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135360493/ 2 sustained major injuries than the petitioner i.e. fractures and bleeding. Further it is contended that, the general public immediately gave water to the petitioner and respondent, started scolding the petitioner for rushing to cross the road. The respondent being an innocent, humble, law abiding citizen did not claim any damages from the petitioner, as he was already in the pain of his injuries. Taking undue advantage of the innocence of respondent, the petitioner has now come up with the present false petition, in order to grab money from the respondent. For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. 5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed: ISSUES 1.
